pack.title: Pop Culture & Wordplay
pack.description: Screen legends, literary surprises, and a twist of language.

categories.title: FILM GENRES
categories.triviaFact: A western typically uses frontier life as a setting for its story.

categories.title: MUSICAL TEMPO DIRECTIONS
categories.triviaFact: Andante suggests a walking pace, while presto calls for a much faster tempo.

categories.title: TRAVELERS TO THE EMERALD CITY
categories.triviaFact: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz began as a novel before its famous screen adaptation.

categories.title: BEFORE STAR
categories.triviaFact: A lodestar is a guiding star, often used metaphorically for a guiding principle.

redHerrings.note: TOTO is also a band's name, but ADAGIO and its partners specify musical speed; the Oz travelers make a complete set.

categories.title: ORCHESTRAL INSTRUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: An oboe produces sound using a double reed made of two thin blades.

categories.title: THEATER WORDS
categories.triviaFact: A play can be divided into acts, which can in turn contain several scenes.

categories.title: FICTIONAL DETECTIVE SURNAMES
categories.triviaFact: Agatha Christie created both Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple.

categories.title: ANAGRAMS OF LISTEN
categories.triviaFact: An anagram rearranges the same letters without adding or removing any.

redHerrings.note: VIOLA is also a Shakespeare character, tempting the theater set, but its precise instrument partners leave four theater terms.

categories.title: FICTIONAL BEARS
categories.triviaFact: Paddington takes his name from the London railway station where he is found.

categories.title: TYPES OF POEM
categories.triviaFact: A traditional sonnet has fourteen lines, though rhyme patterns vary.

categories.title: PEN NAMES
categories.triviaFact: Mark Twain's pen name came from a riverboat expression for measuring water depth.

categories.title: PALINDROMES
categories.triviaFact: A palindrome reads the same in reverse when its letters are kept in order.

redHerrings.note: LIMERICK is a place as well as a poem type, tempting a location link with PADDINGTON, but only the poetry set has four members.

categories.title: DANCE STYLES
categories.triviaFact: A waltz traditionally has three beats to the bar.

categories.title: FILMMAKING JOBS
categories.triviaFact: A gaffer leads the electrical lighting crew on a film production.

categories.title: SHAKESPEARE TRAGEDY TITLES
categories.triviaFact: Hamlet's play within a play is used to test the king's reaction.

categories.title: BEFORE LINE
categories.triviaFact: A punchline delivers the final twist that makes a joke work.

redHerrings.note: CHORUS suggests a stage role beside the film crew, but the four crew jobs are exact; CHORUS forms a phrase with LINE.

categories.title: ONE-WORD PIXAR FILMS
categories.triviaFact: Soul centers on a music teacher who dreams of becoming a professional performer.

categories.title: MUSIC GENRES
categories.triviaFact: Reggae developed in Jamaica and is known for its emphasis on offbeat rhythms.

categories.title: LITERARY NARRATIVE DEVICES
categories.triviaFact: An allegory uses characters or events to convey another layer of meaning.

categories.title: BEGIN AND END WITH THE SAME LETTER
categories.triviaFact: A word can begin and end with the same letter without being a palindrome.

redHerrings.note: SOUL fits naturally beside JAZZ and BLUES, but UP, CARS and BRAVE pin it to the film-title group.

categories.title: WORDS FOR A STORY ENDING
categories.triviaFact: An epilogue can show what happens to characters after the main story ends.

categories.title: FAMOUS FICTIONAL CATS
categories.triviaFact: The Cheshire Cat is known for a grin that can remain after the rest of it disappears.

categories.title: ANAGRAMS OF TEARS
categories.triviaFact: An aster is a flowering plant whose name comes from a Greek word for star.

categories.title: ALSO MEAN TO FINISH
categories.triviaFact: Wrap is used in filmmaking to announce that filming has finished.

redHerrings.note: WRAP could sound like another ending noun, but WRAP, CLOSE, SEAL and COMPLETE are all verbs that can mean to finish.

categories.title: MUSICAL FORMS
categories.triviaFact: A concerto typically contrasts a solo instrument or group with a larger ensemble.

categories.title: CREATURES IN TOLKIEN
categories.triviaFact: Ents are tree-like beings who act as shepherds of the forest in Tolkien's stories.

categories.title: READ DIFFERENTLY AS NOUN AND VERB
categories.triviaFact: English can distinguish a noun from a related verb by changing which syllable is stressed.

categories.title: ADD S AT THE FRONT FOR A NEW WORD
categories.triviaFact: Adding an initial letter can change a word's meaning without changing the order of its other letters.

redHerrings.note: CONDUCT suggests leading a musical performance, but it joins RECORD, PRESENT and OBJECT in changing stress between noun and verb.

categories.title: CLASSIC NOVEL TITLES
categories.triviaFact: Dune imagines a desert planet where control of a valuable resource shapes political power.

categories.title: WORDS THAT IMITATE SOUNDS
categories.triviaFact: Onomatopoeia uses words whose sounds imitate the noises they describe.

categories.title: ANAGRAMS OF SPOT
categories.triviaFact: Short words can have many anagrams because a few letters can form several common arrangements.

categories.title: CAN FOLLOW DOUBLE
categories.triviaFact: A double take is a delayed second look caused by surprise.

redHerrings.note: BASS can suggest a sound beside BUZZ or HISS, but is not an imitation of one; all four partners form DOUBLE expressions.
